# Puzzle Pieces — collection design and solutions

Author document. Contains complete spoilers. The public game never offers these answers as menus.

## Architecture

The entrance faces north along a 19 × 70 metre, 14 metre high hall toward the original abstract statue and tall window. Reception is a curved oak island in the center. A single south-wall stair reaches the west mezzanine only. The east mezzanine requires the employee stair beyond the certified service hall. There are no bridges. The old Security location is now a glass-fronted gift shop. Security has moved into its own small approach hallway south of the public elevator arcade. Six classical marble studies, eight columns and fern planters line the hall; 36 additional abstract paintings occupy public and employee rooms.

The ground-floor route can loop through the Archive of Doubts from the Light Well into the North Arcade. The second secret reaches the northern staff threshold. It does not bypass Security certification. A latch accessible only inside the Absent Room opens a return to the ground-floor hall.

The in-game map omits concealed rooms until their corresponding mechanism has been discovered. The author plan includes all of them. Both plans derive from `layout.js`.

## Security and terrace

The dropped security pass is in the first washroom stall at x=10.4, z=−29.3. Collecting it is a direct interaction. The physical reader releases the office. The handover note connects the suspended weights to the three impressions. Dials must read `○`, `⌜`, `⋈`; all three exhibit seals and the pass must be present. Press the circle to release the north terrace door upstairs.

On the terrace, stand behind the empty frame at x=0, z=−38.4, y=6 and face south toward the museum with a level view for 2.5 seconds. The first-visit ending appears briefly in the scene overlay; exploration remains available. The first-visit ending does not end the new upper or basement puzzles.

## Interaction principles

- Gallery controls operate physically. Computer screens and editable papers open an inspection of their exact world pixels, with click/touch and keyboard access; they are not separate generic puzzle menus.
- The interaction indicator contains no visible name or action text.
- Every card contains the full clue beneath artist and medium. Inspection reuses that visual; selected paintings reuse their exact image.
- Clue images are authored exactly in code. Decorative material generation cannot alter puzzle information.
- Failed access sequences clear their own physical display after a short pause. Recorder entries remain available for correction.
- Wrong deductions are reversible. No limited resource can permanently block progress.
- Original Modern Art saves keep discoveries, settings and notes, while the player returns to the rebuilt entrance.


## Reception, staff areas and lifts

The map and IV brochure are physical collectibles behind the arrival position. The map is available after collection; the brochure remains in carried papers. The bench note and four oriented plants seed a future garden puzzle and are not a current gate.

Security moved south; the dropped washroom credential still opens it. Staff circulation requires accepted redaction work. SOUTH SERVICE additionally requires the accepted Security training sheet. Break-room furnishings and half-size notices moved upstairs. The staff stair continues to the birthday room and administrator’s office on the third floor. The south-wall employees-only door shares the certified service circuit. It connects through a vestibule to the conference room and South Service; the garage and supply closet branch from that hall. The conference-table key opens the gift shop.

The inspection lift at x=12, z=65 connects ground and B1. Return is always available. Its travel is a brief fade and carriage sound, followed by movement to the corresponding landing. The separate freight route at B1 x=−28, z=26 requires clearance; it connects to the upper staff landing at x=31, z=19. Neither lift can strand the player.

## Security — redaction curriculum

Use the washroom card to enter. The Security computer is separate from the three-seal terrace circuit. It displays a white screen with bold black words for the first two calibration lessons. Click a word to cover it, including attached punctuation; click the bar to restore it. Redaction budgets count currently covered words, not gestures. At the limit, an attempted new mark flashes the printed allowance and leaves the sheet intact. Line breaks are whitespace; surviving periods separate statements. Empty or unrecognisable statements cannot pass.

| Sheet | Printed statements | Limit | Redact | Accepted meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| I | `true.` / `false.` | 1 | `false.` including period | `true.` remains. |
| II | `white is not white.` / `black is white.` | 3 | First-line `white.`, second-line `is` and `white.` | Without the first period the lines join: `white is not black`. |
| III | Ordinary `true.` / heavy `black is not white.` | 1 | `not` | Heavy `black is white.` is literally false, inverted to true. |
| IV | `the hall has no windows.` | 1 | `no` | The actual glazing confirms it. |
| V | `cobalt hangs above chalk.` / `below vermilion.` | 2 | `above` and `chalk.` | `cobalt hangs below vermilion.` agrees with the upstairs weights. |
| Final | Ordinary `the hall has no bridge.` / heavy `white is not black.` | 1 | `not` | Both survive; the second is false literally, true after inversion. |

The first five lessons accept immediately, show a green border/check and reveal the bottom arrow. Heavy truth inversion begins on III: the room circular explicitly distinguishes the uniform calibration display weight from the later contrasting heavy register. Hints beside the terminal explain word allowances, attached punctuation, restoration, the weight convention, and where to inspect the suspended colors.

The final sheet must be printed and fed to the nearby physical checker. A wrong sheet travels into the slot and returns after two seconds. The player can revise it in the tray or carried-paper view; retries consume no resource. The submitted snapshot is frozen during checking, duplicate submissions cannot stack, and starting a new game invalidates pending callbacks. Acceptance releases lock 12 to the garage and enables lock 09’s South Service card reader. No original exhibit seals are required. The terrace remains a separate objective.

## Service Garage — language as material

Three connected spaces extend the rear of reception: the service vestibule, concrete garage and timber-floored Letter Workshop. The garage contains a closed loading shutter, an empty van, tyre stacks, crates, work lights and an unclaimed timber frame. Its missing canvas is independent evidence for the dispatch answer.

| Space / gate | Mechanic | Solution and checks | Recovery / outcome |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Security → service wing / 12 | Accepted truth sheet | Final redaction above | Unlocks the service hall, employee stair, garage, conference room and supply closet; the floor cable lights. |
| Garage → workshop / 13 | Five-letter dispatch deduction | `FRAME`; fourteen-word rack register contains the answer. Square = correct place, ring = elsewhere, cross = absent. Matches consume answer letters only once. Empty timber surround confirms the noun. | Six guesses per page; New Page allows unlimited further attempts. |
| Workshop → return passage / 14 | Sixteen loose tiles, four-by-four word square | Rows **CARE / AREA / REAR / EARN**, with identical columns. Every tile used once; C and N fix the opposite corners. Every row/column must occur in the brass register. Exactly one square meets these constraints. | Move, swap or return tiles; checks preserve wrong arrangements. Both concealed corridor doors open on success. |

The return corridor runs north behind Counterform into Hinge Walk, forming a new circulation loop. Garage puzzles are optional after certification and do not gate the first terrace milestone or the lower audit. Their art cards and registers stay in the rooms; no outside dictionary is needed.

## IV — In Perpetuity

Three circular diagrams have six sectors, a red starting seam and an ivory hand. Count the vacant sectors passed clockwise, excluding the occupied sector: **3, 1, 4**. The physical dials open the Afterimage Archive. Independent proof: total 8; first minus second is 2; third minus first is 1. Exactly one triple in 0–5 satisfies that proof.

The Fifth Beat sounds four light ticks and one low beat, with five matching lamps. The reception brochure and physical maker stamp identify P/5 — 2024. The archive explains that the same movement was taken to restoration without authorisation. These are independent ways to identify the suspect watch in B1. The museum does not claim that every historical watch universally used a particular rhythm: the receiving record defines this specific object’s original mechanism.

## V — The Uncatalogued / Lot 409

Three tables hold twelve numbered arrivals; six paired reference paintings show two objects each. These are fictional collection histories. Each object has a physical form, an inspectable exact illustration and a provenance card. Work lights, crates, a waste bin, calibration station, exposed studs, timber, scaffold, tools and packing material establish the unfinished exhibit.

Collect the manifest at the entrance table. I opens carried papers; J opens the manifest. Click/tap a row to cross off or restore it. The paper shares the same Canvas representation in the room and inspector. Marks persist. Submitting freezes the submitted selection for the two-second verifier cycle. A second submission cannot stack. Invalid sheets return without resource loss; gauges A/B/C indicate only whether that table’s group contains an error. The sheet cannot be edited during a cycle or after acceptance. Old callbacks cannot affect a new visit.

| Item | Verdict | Decisive comparison |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 01 Chalice | Retain | Five rubies and a torn claw agree with documented later loss. |
| 02 Astrolabe | Cross off | The engraved 06 reproduces the painter’s recorded mistake; the calibration record requires 90. |
| 03 Vase | Cross off | Surface peeling and a matching numbered stencil contradict the recorded fired underglaze. Nearby paint alone would not prove forgery. |
| 04 Dagger | Cross off | The marked FRONT removes viewpoint ambiguity. The physical left-hand crest copies the mirror image instead of reversing it. |
| 05 Bust | Cross off | Mould seam plus matching WAX / 409-05 sleeve contradict the one-piece carving record. Translucency alone is not treated as proof. |
| 06 Watch | Cross off | Five-pulse P/5 — 2024 movement agrees with the upstairs sculpture, not the documented original sealed four-tick mechanism. |
| 07 Crown | Retain | Bent cross agrees with the low crate lid, matching gold transfer and transit report. |
| 08 Chess queen | Retain | Left sceptre reverses the specific tapestry’s explicitly reversed face. This is a rule of this work, not every tapestry. |
| 09 Mirror | Cross off | Moulded RESIN REPLICA / CAST 2024 underneath the base; a museum barcode by itself would be inconclusive. An inspection mirror and close-up expose it. |
| 10 Lute | Retain | Ten paired courses plus one single string require **21** strings and pegs. The recorded 1890 restringing explains the difference from the painting. |
| 11 Retort | Cross off | 1,420 g and a visible solid core contradict the 310 g hollow-vessel record; a separate weight checks the scale. |
| 12 Guild seal | Retain | The right-facing die produces the left-facing impression. |

Cross off **02, 03, 04, 05, 06, 09, 11**. Retain **01, 07, 08, 10, 12**. Exactly one of the 4,096 binary manifests is accepted. Clearance opens the freight door and appears among carried papers. The five-contact circuit accepts the retained accession numbers in ascending order: **1 → 7 → 8 → 10 → 12**. This illuminates the lower circuit. Wrong entries are reversible.

The quarantine introduction, provenance records, exact object illustrations and independent environmental corroboration together define the audit. Neither outside historical research nor an actual telephone call is required.

The future garden installation, carried restoration tools and museum transformations remain in [EXHIBIT-ROADMAP.md](EXHIBIT-ROADMAP.md).


## Circulation revision and new collection

The south stair is public and ends at the west mezzanine. Redaction lesson V now points to the public Three Suspensions study on that ledge, avoiding a dependency on the still-locked employee floor. The washroom card opens Security only. Correct final work in the checker releases both the South Service threshold and the south-wall employee door. A visible copper floor cable traces computer → office doorway → service door and lights on acceptance.

From South Service, players reach the inspection lift to B1, garage, supply closet, conference room and employee stair. The employee stair reaches a long upper corridor, then the existing Employee Hall, loft, Lantern Walk and east mezzanine. The original northern stairs remain internal circulation to the third floor; their ground door waits for certification.

The two public cars in the South Arcade begin isolated. Players first climb the employee stair and physically restore PUBLIC LIFT SUPPLY upstairs. Calls then open the sliding doors and the interior button travels between Ground and Upper. B1 uses the separate service lift; freight requires manifest clearance.

The gift shop is visible through the hall-side glass but locked initially. Its tagged brass key sits on the conference table; collecting it releases the shop and adds its key card to inventory. No purchase or additional puzzle is needed.

There are 36 new original abstract works across color-field, gesture, construction, veil, point, collage, contour, weave, erasure, arc, relief and stripe/wave treatments. Six Greek-inspired sculpture studies have provenance cards. These atmospheric additions are inspectable and do not add hidden numerical locks. The atlas distinguishes their role from the active exhibit puzzles.
